text:
lina: anyone else seeing a sharp tail-latency bump on eu-west dedicated GPUs? 99th is ~3x since 03:20 UTC

sam: saw it. correlates with sustained egress bursts from tenant tf-batch-231 (large dataset pulls) :thinking_face:

kai: do we have host-level metrics? nvlink/kvcache misses?

lina: quick dump from 10s ago — nvlink wait and TX drops up on rack-12 top-of-rack
```
node-12a: nvlink_wait_ms: 12 -> 85
node-12a: tx_errors: 0 -> 42
node-12a: egress_bytes/s: 120MB -> 820MB
```

michelle: if that tenant is doing heavy remote reads, it will trample shared egress. is this on dedicated pool or shared-slices?

sam: dedicated-pool (eu-west-dedicated-3). We pinned a few enterprise customers there last month. tf-batch got scheduled across 4 nodes.

kai: ok, noisy neighbor peak on dedicated = bad. Two options: hard carveout (reserve extra racks) or soft-isolate (per-tenant egress qdisc + routing preference). Hard carveout = +capex/opcost.

michelle: i'll run numbers but rough: carving another 10% capacity for isolation would increase committed spend ~15% q/q given current utilization. Not great for customer cost.

lina: I prototyped a soft-isolate qdisc on a canary node earlier — applied `tc` egress shaping per cgroup and bumped local cache preference. Tail dropped ~70% for our test workload. Caveat: dataset pulls that hit S3 still blow past when they stream >600MB/s.

sam: can you paste the `tc` rule?

lina: sure — used simple HTB + fq_codel with per-tenant class and a 200MB/s ceiling
```bash
# canary example
tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 10
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 1gbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 200mbit ceil 200mbit
tc filter add dev eth0 protocol ip parent 1:0 prio 1 handle 101 cgroup
```

kai: nice. That looks non-invasive. We should be careful with latency-sensitive RPCs — fq limits help. Did you observe CPU side effects?

lina: minor CPU bump (~2%) for `tc` bookkeeping. Acceptable on our nodes.

michelle: policy question — are we ok shipping soft-isolate as platform default for dedicated? customers might expect no throttling. We need config opt-out or an SLA note.

sam: propose: enable soft-isolate by default, but for customers who pay for "hard isolation" we reserve racks (explicit carveout) and advertise tail SLO. Also add automated fallback: if qdisc can't keep tail under SLO, route new allocs to reserve pool.

kai: that's a good hybrid. Action items:
- enable soft-isolate canary on rack-12 (eu-west) this afternoon (sam/lina)
- add metric for per-tenant egress shaping hits and SLO breaches (lina)
- cost model for 10% carveout vs. recurring throttling impact (michelle)
- upgrade rollout doc + opt-out flag for enterprise roll (sam)

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-4532 — "eu-west dedicated egress tail spike". Pager duty notified.

michelle: putting cost calc on my calendar, will share rough delta by EOD.

sam: i'll prepare the canary roll steps. if we get a clean reduction, we can push region-wide but keep carveout as a paid option. :thumbsup:

kai: +1. also let's capture a short-runbook for when qdisc causes unexpected regressions (rollback `tc qdisc del dev eth0 root`).

lina: noted — will push PR with scripts and dashboards.

sam: thanks all — keeping this thread as the coordination log. ping me if you see regressions after the canary.
